epithet.en: The future Richard III, the play's villain-hero

1.modern-en: Richard opens the play with the soliloquy 'Now is the winter of our discontent,' tricks Clarence into the Tower, and lays out his plan to take the throne.

2.modern-en: Richard intercepts Henry VI's funeral procession in the street and woos Lady Anne over the corpse of her father-in-law.

3.modern-en: Richard insults Queen Elizabeth in open court, is cursed at length by Queen Margaret, and orders the murderers to the Tower.

5.modern-en: Richard joins the dying Edward IV's bedside, reports Clarence dead, and watches the king collapse.

6.modern-en: Richard is referred to in the Duchess of York's lament for her sons.

8.modern-en: Richard offstage manoeuvres against the queen's family while Elizabeth flees with her son to sanctuary.

9.modern-en: Richard greets the young prince Edward and arranges to lodge him in the Tower with his brother.

10.modern-en: Richard sends Catesby to sound out Hastings and lays the trap for him.

12.modern-en: Richard interrupts the council on the boy king's coronation, accuses Hastings of treason, and has him led off to immediate execution.

13.modern-en: Richard shows himself in armour on the Tower walls with the Mayor and explains the supposed plot against him.

14.modern-en: Richard sends a scrivener through London with a backdated indictment of Hastings to be read out.

15.modern-en: Richard puts on a show of piety at Baynard's Castle and accepts the crown only after Buckingham 'begs' him.

16.modern-en: Richard, now king, sets aside Anne for a new match and asks Buckingham to murder the princes in the Tower.

17.modern-en: Richard finds Buckingham reluctant, dismisses him, and arranges with Tyrrel to do the deed.

18.modern-en: Richard orders his current wife Anne quietly disposed of and sets his eyes on his niece, Elizabeth's daughter.

19.modern-en: Richard confronts the Duchess of York and Elizabeth in the street and is cursed by both, then attempts to woo Elizabeth for her daughter.

21.modern-en: Richard receives the news at Salisbury of Buckingham's capture and orders him executed without an audience.

23.modern-en: Richard pitches camp at Bosworth, dines with his commanders, and goes to bed.

24.modern-en: Richard sleeps and is visited by the ghosts of every person he has murdered; he wakes calling for a horse and Jesus together.

25.modern-en: Richard rallies his army with a final speech, is unhorsed in the battle, cries 'A horse, a horse, my kingdom for a horse,' and is killed by Richmond.

epithet.en: Widow of Edward Prince of Wales, later Richard's queen

2.modern-en: Anne walks behind Henry VI's corpse cursing Richard, and is wooed by him over the body until she accepts his ring.

16.modern-en: Anne is summoned to Richard's coronation, dreads becoming his queen, and is conducted off to be quietly removed.

epithet.en: Widow of Henry VI, the cursing queen of the previous war

3.modern-en: Margaret enters the council chamber unannounced and lays a long, detailed curse on Richard, the queen, and the king's family.

19.modern-en: Margaret reappears in old mourning to gloat to Elizabeth and the Duchess of York as her curses come true one by one.

epithet.en: Edward IV's queen, mother of the young princes

3.modern-en: Elizabeth is insulted by Richard at court and warned by Margaret of what is coming.

5.modern-en: Elizabeth attends her dying husband and is told of Clarence's death.

8.modern-en: Elizabeth, hearing that Richard has seized her family, flees with her younger son into the sanctuary of Westminster Abbey.

16.modern-en: Elizabeth stands at the Tower as her son is taken from her, and gives him up only after being forced.

19.modern-en: Elizabeth, mother of two murdered princes, refuses Richard's marriage offer for her daughter in a long, bitter exchange.

3.modern-en: Buckingham is at the council chamber and joins Richard in baiting Margaret.

5.modern-en: Buckingham helps stage the meeting between the young king's party and Richard.

9.modern-en: Buckingham greets the young prince Edward at the city walls with elaborate ceremony.

12.modern-en: Buckingham is seated at the council that condemns Hastings.

13.modern-en: Buckingham rouses the Mayor and citizens to support Richard's claim.

14.modern-en: Buckingham takes the dossier of Hastings's supposed crimes to be made public.

15.modern-en: Buckingham stage-manages the show at Baynard's Castle, presenting Richard to the citizens as a reluctant candidate.

16.modern-en: Buckingham listens, with growing reluctance, as Richard asks him to murder the princes.

17.modern-en: Buckingham hesitates over the murder, asks Richard for his promised reward, and is brushed off.

21.modern-en: Buckingham is brought as a prisoner before the new king and led to immediate execution.

epithet.en: The Tudor claimant, the future Henry VII

22.modern-en: Richmond marches across England gathering forces and speaks to his commanders about the cause.

23.modern-en: Richmond pitches camp opposite Richard at Bosworth and confers with his lieutenants.

24.modern-en: Richmond, blessed in his dreams by the ghosts of Richard's victims, rises to give the dawn battle speech.

25.modern-en: Richmond kills Richard in single combat, accepts the crown, and pledges peace by marrying Elizabeth's daughter.

epithet.en: Richard's older brother, betrayed in Act 1

1.modern-en: Clarence is led to the Tower under guard and is told by Richard with great show of sympathy that the king must be made to relent.

4.modern-en: Clarence, in the Tower, tells Brakenbury his ominous dream and is then murdered by two assassins; one drowns him in a barrel of malmsey wine.

1.modern-en: Hastings is brought from the Tower at the play's opening, released by the king's command.

10.modern-en: Hastings receives Catesby's overtures and refuses to back Richard's claim to the throne.

11.modern-en: Hastings rides cheerfully to the council, taking the messenger's warning of dreams as superstition.

12.modern-en: Hastings is accused of treason at the council by Richard, sentenced on the spot, and led out to be beheaded.

epithet.en: Edward V and his younger brother, the boys in the Tower

9.modern-en: The boy king Edward V is met outside London by Richard and Buckingham and brought to lodge in the Tower with his small brother.

16.modern-en: The younger prince is fetched from sanctuary and joined with his brother in the Tower; both will be smothered before Act 4 ends.

epithet.en: Mother of Edward IV, Clarence, and Richard

5.modern-en: The Duchess of York mourns the death of her son Clarence's children's father with Queen Elizabeth.

16.modern-en: The Duchess stands at the Tower as Elizabeth's son is taken from her and laments the family she has lost.

19.modern-en: The Duchess curses Richard in the street, calls him her shame, and joins Elizabeth and Margaret in their litany of grief.
